questions.question: A function `f <- function(v, k) { ... }` is defined at the console, and the call `f(a, 2)` starts. Before the first line of the body runs, what does the new local environment of this call contain?
options: Copies of every object in the global environment, ready for the body to change
The arguments `v` and `k`, holding the values passed in this call
The objects that the previous call of `f` created in its body
Nothing yet; `v` and `k` are looked up in the global environment

questions.question: To set a global object back to zero, a student defines `reset <- function() { counter <- 0 }` and then runs `counter <- 5; reset(); counter`. R prints `[1] 5`. Why?
options: `reset()` must receive `counter` as an argument before it can change it
The assignment in the body runs only when the result of `reset()` is printed
The function did change `counter`, but R shows the value saved before the call
`counter <- 0` in the body creates a local `counter`, removed when the call ends

questions.question: In a fresh RStudio session, `x <- 3; f <- function(y) { z <- x + y; z }; f(4)` is run at the console. Which objects does the Environment pane list afterwards?
options: `x` and `f`
`x`, `f`, `y` and `z`
`x`, `f` and `z`
`x`, `f` and `y`

questions.question: The function `g <- function(y) x + y` uses an object `x` that it neither receives nor creates. Why is `g2 <- function(x, y) x + y` the safer design?
options: `g2` runs faster, since R does not have to search the global environment
`g` cannot be called at all while an object `x` exists in the global environment
The result of `g2` depends only on its arguments, not on what a global `x` holds
`g2` updates the global `x` on each call, so the global value is kept current

questions.question: With a global object `x <- 100` in the session, the function `f <- function(x) x + 1` is defined. What does `f(5)` return?
options: an error, as `x` is already a global object

questions.question: What does R print for the last line of `rate <- 0.05; interest <- function(amount) amount * rate; a <- interest(200); rate <- 0.1; c(a, interest(200))`?
options: the error `object 'rate' not found`

questions.question: In a fresh session, what does R print for the last line of `f <- function(v) { tmp <- v * 2; tmp + 1 }; f(4); tmp`?
options: the error `object 'tmp' not found`
`NULL`

questions.question: What does R print for the last line of `i <- 100; f <- function() { for (i in 1:3) { }; i }; f(); i`?
options: the error `object 'i' not found`

questions.question: In a fresh session, `p <- function(n) n * k` is defined and `p(2)` is called. No object `k` exists anywhere. What happens?
options: R stops with the error `object 'k' not found`
R stops with the error `argument "k" is missing, with no default`
R returns `[1] 0`, treating the unknown `k` as 0
R returns `[1] NA`, treating the unknown `k` as missing

questions.question: What does R print for `c(h(a), a)` after `a <- c(5, 6); h <- function(a) { a[1] <- 0; sum(a) }`?
options: an error, since an argument cannot be changed in the body

questions.question: The function `h <- function(v) { v[2] <- 0; v }` returns a changed copy of its argument. After `a <- c(4, 5, 6)`, which line makes `a` itself hold the values 4, 0 and 6?
A function defined at the console uses the name `w` in its body. In which order does R search for `w` when the function is called?
options: First the global environment, then the call's arguments and local objects; then it stops with an error
Only among the call's arguments; any other name stops the call with an error
First the call's arguments and local objects, then the global environment; then it stops with an error
First the call's arguments and local objects, then the global environment; then it uses `NA`

questions.question: To make `g <- function(y) x + y` independent of the global environment, a student adds `x <- x` as the first line of its body. With a global `x <- 3`, `g(4)` returns 7; after `x <- 10`, it returns 14. Why did the extra line not help?
options: R skips the line, since it ignores an assignment of a name to itself
The line changes the global `x` to itself, so it has no effect on `g`
The local `x` is created once, when `g` is defined, and is then updated
The right-hand `x` is still read from the global environment at each call

questions.question: What does R print for `c(add(), add(), n)` after `n <- 0; add <- function() { n <- n + 1; n }`?
Both functions are defined at the console: `x <- 1; g <- function() x * 10; h <- function() { x <- 2; g() }`. What does `h()` return?
options: `NULL`
the error `object 'x' not found`

questions.question: With a global object `x <- 5`, the function `f <- function(x) x * 2` is called as `f()`, without an argument. What happens?
options: R returns `[1] 10`, using the global `x`
R stops with the error `argument "x" is missing, with no default`
R returns `[1] NA`, since the missing argument is `NA`
R stops with the error `object 'x' not found`

questions.question: A function `f` is defined at the console, and its body uses only its arguments and objects it has assigned earlier in the same body. Which statement about calls of `f` is correct?
options: `f` returns the same value for every call, whatever the arguments are
`f` can never stop with an error, since every name it uses is defined
Equal arguments give equal results, whatever global objects exist
Each call of `f` updates the global objects that share the names of its locals

questions.question: A function `inner` is created inside the body of another function `outer`, and `inner` uses a name `x` that is neither its argument nor assigned in its own body. Where does R look for `x` next?
options: In the local environment of the call of `outer` that created `inner`
Directly in the global environment, as it does for every function
In the environment of whichever function happens to call `inner`
Nowhere: `inner` may use only its own arguments and local objects

questions.question: After `y <- 5; f <- function(x) { if (x > 0) y <- 1; y * 10 }`, what does `c(f(2), f(-2))` return?
options: the error `object 'y' not found`, raised by `f(-2)`

questions.question: What does R print for `c(f(x + 1), x)` after `x <- 1; f <- function(y) { x <- 100; y }`?
